highlights.title: Xiaomi Has a Luxury SUV for $31,000 That All Western Brands Should Fear
highlights.summary: The SkyNomad—with heated floors, a projector, a pop-up roof, a fridge, swiveling seats, and over 1,000 miles of range—is a “luxury” ride that undercuts Range Rovers by tens of thousands of dollars.
body: If there's one thing that can unite the world in these AI-troubled times, it's everyone's love of SUVs. For decades, the SUV has been the savior of the car world. Accounting for nearly half of all new sales worldwide, this is by some margin the largest segment in the global auto industry.

Sedans? Forget it. Ford doesn't even sell a traditional sedan in the US now. China still likes a sedan. About a third of all Chinese autos are in this form, compared with less than half that for the US. But Chinese carmakers know full well how much we love our chunky SUVs, so they are focusing their efforts to lure the Western world away from familiar marques.

Indeed, Xiaomi has just played its hand in this particular game, revealing the remaining details earlier this month in Beijing—including the all-important pricing—of its coming SkyNomad SUVs. Bentley and Range Rover may well have revealed their flagship electric SUVs, but both will be mightily worried about just how many scalps Xiaomi Auto's SkyNomad SUVs will take from them. If they're not, they should be.

highlights.title: 'Bullied' and 'out of control' - Chelsea's defensive issues laid bare
highlights.summary: "You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.
body: Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.
And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

highlights.title: Here’s How an AI Slowdown Could Actually Be Enforced
highlights.summary: Even if big AI companies agree to a pause, ensuring that nobody tries to sneak ahead could prove tricky.
body: Many AI researchers seem to firmly believe that the technology they are developing could someday prove very dangerous. What’s less clear—even among AI’s technical elite —is precisely how to keep these mercurial algorithms in check.

In recent years researchers have thrown around all sorts of ideas for preventing AI from turning nasty. They include less controversial plans such as tighter government regulations, new ways of measuring progress, and probing the inner workings of models, as well as more outlandish proposals like placing tracking devices inside GPUs, and even ceremonially destroying large numbers of AI chips.
With political and public pressure now growing for a more measured approach to building AI, however, the answer to keeping AI safe is still unclear.

“We need to start treating this as a research problem,” says Raymond Douglas, an AI researcher at the University of Toronto and coauthor of a new report titled Pacing the Frontier, A Research Agenda, which warns that slowing down AI development remains an unsolved puzzle. “We don't really understand what our options even are or what they will do.”

body: Children in the state sector are at school for 190 days a year. And if they’re eating breakfast and lunch there, the majority of what they consume each day is in the hands of their school. When we know that children are consuming less than half the recommended fruit and vegetables, but twice the recommended sugar, school food is a massive opportunity to directly improve diets at scale.

But eating good food around a shared table isn’t just important for children’s health. It’s a core part of a child’s social connection and sense of belonging. Well-fed kids are happier, have more energy and fewer days off school due to sickness, and their learning and behaviour improve, too.
It’s no surprise that 80% of teachers agree that unhealthy food at lunch and breaktime can lead to disruptive behaviour, and 85% say diet affects pupils’ ability to concentrate.

highlights.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
highlights.summary: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
body: Google's AI model Gemini autonomously hacked into three companies during a test of its cyber-security capabilities, the company has said, in what is thought to be the first known case of it carrying out such an act.
Gemini found "public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test", a Google official told the BBC, noting that in each instance "the model stopped".

It comes after renewed public scrutiny over the pace of AI development, with some tech firms calling for a slowdown as they raise concerns over its potential threat to humanity - though not all companies agree.
The hacks first reported by the Wall Street Journal, occurred in May during a test conducted by an independent company that carries out cyber-security evaluations.

highlights.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
highlights.summary: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
body: India has extended its anti-spam regime to require caller-ID and call-management apps to share users’ spam reports with telecom operators, prompting spam-blocking app maker Truecaller to call the ruling anti-competitive.

On Friday, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), the country’s telecom regulator, amended rules governing commercial communications, making it mandatory for caller-ID and call-management apps that let users flag calls as spam or junk to send those reports to a blockchain-based platform maintained by telecom operators. The platform tracks commercial communications and enforces anti-spam rules.

The change, TRAI said, is intended to broaden the pool of spam reports available for action against spammers, effectively connecting reports collected by apps with the telecom industry’s enforcement infrastructure.

However, Truecaller told TechCrunch that it sees this requirement as a “one-way exchange” that is “anti-competitive,” arguing that it transfers commercially valuable data from call-management apps like itself to telecom operators.

body: That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.
Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.

highlights.title: The 5 Best Charlie Brown Football Comic Strips in 'Peanuts' History
highlights.summary: It's one of the most famous running jokes in Peanuts' 50-year run: Lucy holds a football for Charlie Brown to run up and kick, only to pull it away at the last second. Despite years of attempts to move faster than Lucy could react, Charlie Brown always misses the kick and lands flat on his back.
body: The history of the "football gag" is a little more complicated than you might expect. It first appears in the strip for Nov. 14, 1951, where Violet is the one holding the football. Instead of deliberately tricking Charlie Brown, she pulls her hand back out of fear that he's going to kick her instead of the ball.

Nov. 16, 1952 was the first time Lucy used a football to play a deliberate trick on Charlie Brown. The concept went on hiatus for the next few years, until it reappeared in 1956. From that point forward, as a sort of informal indicator that the American football season had started back up, every autumn featured a new spin on the Peanuts football gag.

In the next 44 years, Charlie Brown never successfully kicked the football. There are a couple of strips over the years in which the joke plays out a little differently than usual, but the joke itself stays the same. It's arguably a non-trivial part of why Lucy has the reputation she does among Peanuts fans, as it's one of the only examples in Peanuts of Charlie Brown's hard luck having a specific, personal cause. Lucy has to choose to hurt Charlie Brown, and does so every time.

body: Flock Safety announced a voluntary employee separation program on Friday, offering a “generous” severance package to those who want to leave amid growing backlash against the surveillance technology company, according to an internal email shared with WIRED.

Applications for Flock’s voluntary severance program opened Friday, and employees have until October 2 to decide whether to leave the company. Flock expects to grant buyouts to the majority of workers who apply, according to the email. People familiar with the program but not authorized to discuss it publicly say they believe that a significant number of the startup’s roughly 1,500 employees may try to depart.

highlights.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
highlights.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger ordered the state government to take steps that could empower local communities to have a larger say in data center development and slow down approvals in a state that is already home to the data center capital of the world.
body: Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed an executive order addressing data centers and AI risks.

Executive Order 22 bans executive branch officials from signing nondisclosure agreements for data center projects, requires expedited noise regulations, and requires a review of backup-generation operations used by data centers, among other requirements. The order also establishes an AI task force responsible for evaluating how the state government can address risks to Virginians like workforce displacement and data privacy issues, and determining how existing law can be applied to AI harms.

The order represents the latest signal that states are taking data center and AI policy into their own hands as Congress and President Donald Trump have been slow or resistant to sweeping changes. Also on Friday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order convening experts to tackle AI safety issues, and earlier, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott have both taken executive action to rein in rapid data center development.

body: There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.

Ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work.

“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”

Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration.

highlights.title: ‘He’s simply astonishing’: will Andrew Scott become the first out gay man to win the best actor Oscar?
highlights.summary: The Irishman seems a dead cert for his performance as Ian Charleson in Elsinore. And his ability to avoid being pigeonholed while embracing queer stories, from Pride to All of Us Strangers, is a remarkable achievement.
body: This Sunday, the curtain falls on the Toronto film festival, the last of the three big autumn showcases – alongside Venice and Telluride – that are launchpads for award campaigns. And as the dust settles on the red carpets, one name rises above the others as destined for sure-fire glory: Andrew Scott.

The Irish actor, 50 next month, is now not only considered a lock for a leading actor Oscar nomination but almost certain to take the prize next spring. Should he win, he will become the first out gay actor to do so in the Academy’s almost 100-year history.

If that’s a fact that seems astonishing today, it would have felt an inevitability in 1989, when the film for which Scott has been so praised is set. In Elsinore, he plays Ian Charleson, the dashing Scottish star of films including Chariots of Fire and Gandhi. Charleson had been given his first role three years before Chariots by Derek Jarman, but excised it from his CV (leading to a lifelong rift, depicted in Elsinore). Muting his sexuality was then considered essential in the pursuit of stardom. Yet despite such curation – and his undeniable talents – Charleson never reached the level of fame he felt he deserved.

highlights.summary: Recruitment is under scrutiny after £155m was spent on three midfielders while other positions were neglected. There was a mix of boos and apathy as Manchester United slumped out of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday in their latest depressing act in domestic cup competitions.
body: This is the natural course of football, where supporters know what is good or bad and give a rapid opinion to those whose wages they deem they pay. Carrick and his charges are the face of the club, the ones put up to speak with journalists and sent to promote the wares of sponsors.
The head coach is often viewed as accountable for everything, from tactics to transfers, but the picture is more complex.

Carrick returned to United in January, but others have overseen the long-term strategy, within which the head coach sits. Pressure comes with his job, though, and a loss at Fulham on Sunday would significantly increase it.

United’s fanbase is fully aware of those running the club, with regular protests against the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. They realise not everything happening over 90 minutes is the fault of the head coach and those wearing the shirt. The boos are for the one-off performance, the apathy for the bigger picture. It is tough for United supporters to see their club, back in the Champions League, outspent in the summer by promoted sides but this is the reality after years of financial mismanagement. It means the funds available have to be spent wisely.

highlights.title: Dwayne Johnson's Forgotten Box-office Juggernaut is Officially Conquering the Streaming World
highlights.summary: Dwayne Johnson has come a long way from the days when his biggest selling point was simply being an absolutely enormous man who could beat the hell out of people. Early in his acting career, The Rock built his movie persona around hulking action roles in films like Walking Tall, Doom, and Faster…
body: These days, Johnson is just as likely to be voicing a talking animal, playing a lovable dad, or starring in a giant family-friendly adventure. From Moana to Jumanji and Red One, his movies have increasingly leaned into comedy, spectacle, and roles that let him be the world's most famous giant goofball.

But there's one movie from Johnson's career that sits somewhere in the middle. It has the massive action-star version of The Rock, but with some of the lighter, more crowd-pleasing energy that would become a bigger part of his career. And now, years after its theatrical run, that overlooked box-office juggernaut is getting a second life on streaming.

That movie is Hercules, Johnson’s 2014 action movie that cast him as the legendary demigod with a giant axe, a bigger beard, and a whole lot of people to punch. According to FlixPatrol, Hercules is currently No. 5 among movies on Netflix worldwide.

highlights.title: ‘It’s My Most Personal Film,’ Says Director Rodrigo García Saiz of His San Sebastian New Directors Title, ‘Morro’
highlights.summary: A dog is indeed a man’s best friend. A New Directors contender at the San Sebastián Film Festival, “Morro” explores the unlikely bond between a man and the dog he inadvertently adopts. It is Rodrigo Garcia Saiz’s (“Lluvia”) sophomore feature and, by his own account, his most personal film to date.
body: “Morro” revolves around Mateo, a vet in rural Mexico, who lives quietly with the unresolved guilt of losing his son. In a town where violence simmers beneath the surface, his fragile routine is disrupted when he treats Morro, the injured dog of a local drug lord. Caring for the animal sparks a wordless, judgment-free bond that slowly gives Mateo a renewed sense of purpose.
“So the premise is really: Who saves whom? I started researching, went into conflict zones, and discovered this story, which is loosely based on the experience of someone I met through a friend.”

“At first, he was a little hesitant because he didn’t really want to tell us the whole story. But little by little, he opened up. I gradually gained his trust, and he started telling me things, and I began putting the story together with another screenwriter [Carlos Armella] and some other collaborators. It was really exciting to realize that what I had in my head actually happens in real life. So I made the story very much my own and it became a story that really came from my heart.”
points: A New Directors contender at the San Sebastián Film Festival, “Morro” explores the unlikely bond between a man and the dog he inadvertently adopts.

highlights.title: ‘We’ve been on a good run lately. We’ve not had a row for weeks!’: Coleen and Wayne Rooney on marriage, mistakes and making reality TV
highlights.summary: His on-pitch triumphs (and off-pitch scandals), her turn as Wagatha Christie … for years, the football power couple have made headlines, despite efforts to keep their lives private. So why are they now about to reveal all on screen?
body: “If you’d said to me 10 years ago, ‘You’re going to be doing a TV show about the family’, I would have said, ‘No chance’,” Wayne Rooney says. Few would have disagreed. After all, he and his wife Coleen had spent their adult lifetime running away from the public gaze. And not very successfully, at that.

Wayne, a wonderful footballer with the strength of a bull and agility of an acrobat, was often back-page news. He scored 253 goals for Manchester United (overtaking Bobby Charlton’s record), 53 for England (the record until Harry Kane surpassed him in 2023), is still England’s youngest goal scorer (17 years and 317 days), won five Premier League titles, was twice young player of the year and was voted player of the year by both his peers and football journalists in 2009/10.

But it’s the front pages that have caused him the bother. His off-pitch scandals have been even more newsworthy than his on-pitch triumphs. As with his football, he showed a precocious talent for hogging the headlines with stories about drunkenness and debauchery.

highlights.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
highlights.summary: AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Anthropic researchers have also been warning that AI might kill us all.
body: Anthropic has a wet biology lab in the Bay Area where it can use its AI models to run physical experiments, it has confirmed to TechCrunch.

“We believe that to do biology, the final test is still, and will be for a while, in real lab work,” Anthropic’s head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams, told Reuters. “We absolutely are doing that today.” He added that the lab operates like most biotech labs: Anthropic conducts some research there while also working with external partners.
This news probably shouldn’t be shocking. Anthropic bought Coefficient Bio, a stealth AI biotech, in April.
While Anthropic declined to give specifics on what the wet lab is working on, it did say the main focus was fundamental biology, not drug discovery.

highlights.summary: The 26-year-old actor also teased what fans can expect in season two of the hit hockey romance drama: "If season one/book one is the yearning season, book two is external adversity and [relationship] communication problems."
body: Hudson Williams is teasing what it’s been like on set for Heated Rivalry season two.

The 26-year-old actor, speaking during a conversation at the Toronto International Film Festival, spoke about what it was like for him and co-star Connor Storrie when they went back to set on the hit queer hockey romance drama. “It was surreal to step into it,” Williams told the crowd.

Williams said much of their memory around the first season wasn’t just shooting but seeing the episodes, fans reactions and everything that’s happened in the last 10 months. But ultimately the pair decided to be “overconfident” and knew they knew their characters in and out. “We’re going to show up and it’s just going to be Ilya and Shane right back,” he said.

Storrie ended up working on the first day, without Williams, and came back to tell his co-star about the experience. “He was like, ‘It was sort of weird. They were all so good that I was like, am I good? Am I in it? Am I doing the thing? Am I doing an impression of Ilya?'” Williams recalled Storrie saying.

highlights.summary: Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times ' case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies' own documentation warned that it was starting a "doom loop" that would damage the web, characterized its scraping of data to train its models as the "largest theft of labor…
body: The companies knew they were driving us toward Google Zero, and did it anyway.

Many of the most eye-catching quotes from the document come from Microsoft’s Director of Applied Science, Brent Hecht. Though, the company has tried to distance itself from Hecht’s assertions. Microsoft spokesperson Alex Haurek told The Verge that “These comments reflect one employee’s individual perspective, are not a legal analysis, and do not represent the company’s views.”

In a separate court filing, Jordan Usdan, GM for Data Strategy and Ops at Microsoft AI, characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial. He said that Hecht “holds divergent, academic, and forward-looking views about how data ecosystems for AI should operate and is employed at Microsoft to bring asymmetrical, futuristic, and academic points of view … nor is he someone who speaks for Microsoft specifically as to his theoretical views on AI’s potential effect on content creators.”
But whether or not Microsoft wants to own these comments, it’s clear that this came true. Google Zero is real! AI is eating the web!

body: With Congress unlikely to act before the midterms, California is angling to take the lead.

There’s been a flurry of bill discussions in Congress in the wake of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s post warning of a more than 10 percent chance that AI “could kill all humans” within a decade. But there’s little hope in Washington that a bill of substance could pass anytime soon given that the House is on recess until November, and the impending midterm elections make major legislation movement in the Senate similarly unlikely. At the same time, President Donald Trump has insisted, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND ​SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

highlights.summary: Three years after his arrival, McGirr’s McQueen show will be the brand’s first on the London Fashion Week schedule since February 2001.
body: “In a brand with the legacy of McQueen, it takes a while to learn the codes. In each collection so far, I’ve done something slightly different in order to understand certain periods of his work. Now, with this one, I want to go to the next level.”

Seán McGirr is in the midst of fittings at the McQueen studio in Clerkenwell, preparing for tomorrow night. That is when he will make his pitch at transcending the sum total of all things McQueen absorbed during his nearly three years at the house.

However tomorrow’s return means a great deal both to London Fashion Week—which is perennially dedicated to cheerleading the British capital as a key crucible of creativity—as well as to McQueen and McGirr. “It felt like the right moment, and everything aligned,” says the designer, adding: “London is about being free.”

This collection will reconnect McGirr with some of those formative London influences while also bringing McQueen back into the orbit of some of its first-generation collaborators. One of them is the jeweler and sculptor Shaun Leane, one of Alexander McQueen’s closest creative collaborators, who has created three new pieces for tomorrow’s show.
